newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 75 cts down, Brent about 5 cts up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 75 cts down, Brent about 5 cts up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open narrowly lower on Wednesday but Brent crude should rebound from a new 12-month low posted in late trade, shrugging off U.S. inventory data, dealers said.

June gas oil is seen opening 50 cents to $1 down from its closing price of $161.50 a tonne while July Brent should track Singapore higher, adding about five cents to its London close of $17.50 a barrel.
Dealers said American Petroleum Institute (API) data released late Tuesday showing rising crude and product inventories would have little immediate impact.
"The APIs are pretty neutral for Brent. Most people were expecting builds of a greater magnitude," said a broker.

U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage rose 336,000 barrels in the week ended June 6. Distillate stocks rose 1.94 million barrels and gasoline stocks increased by 2.71 million barrels, the API said.

Rising gasoline stocks could result in further downward pressure when U.S. markets open later on Wednesday but Brent crude was unlikely to buckle, despite briefly piercing long-term technical support and falling to $17.45 a barrel, the lowest prompt value since May 20, 1996.
